hook: Four hundred seventeen pairs. That was all.
caption: You think of bald eagles as a given. They weren't. In 1963 the entire contiguous United States held four hundred seventeen nesting pairs. DDT was thinning their eggshells to the point where mothers crushed their own clutches just by sitting on them. The pesticide was banned in 1972. The Endangered Species Act passed in 1973. Both were written with this bird in mind. The population recovered to over seventy thousand nesting pairs by 2020. Ben Franklin, for the record, called the bald eagle a bird of bad moral character. The Continental Congress put it on the national seal anyway. It became the symbol of a country that almost let it vanish.
